issue.title: Prune or rotate the three append-only TUI stores backing SASE CONTEXT enrichment
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-l6.6 (land phase of epic sase-l6, SASE CONTEXT incremental enrichment); named as follow-up 1 in plans:202608/sase_context_incremental.md.

Epic sase-l6 (bead sase-l6.2, 'stores') added process-wide revalidating snapshot caches for the artifact-file index (~/.sase/artifacts/index.jsonl), the memory-read log, and the skill-use log, so N agents now share one parse per store change instead of paying a full re-read each. That fixed defect 1 (repeated whole-store parses) but the stores themselves remain append-only and unpruned:

  ~/.sase/artifacts/index.jsonl                          7.68 MB / 7,747 rows (2026-08-13 baseline)
  ~/.sase/projects/gh_sase-org__sase/memory_reads.jsonl  2.73 MB / 4,164 rows
  ~/.sase/projects/gh_sase-org__sase/skill_uses.jsonl    3.09 MB / 6,222 rows

All three grow with every hour of SASE usage, so even a single warm parse (now amortized across agents, not eliminated) gets slower over time, and the epic's land-phase re-measurement (2026-08-14) confirms the underlying files are larger still.

Scope: decide and implement a retention policy per store (prune, rotate to cold storage, or age out), consistent with each store's read/write paths in src/sase/core/artifact_file_explicit.py, src/sase/ace/tui/memory_reads.py, and src/sase/ace/tui/skill_uses.py.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-kh — a differently-scoped prune/archive task for the agent-artifact index sqlite DB used by ACE startup/agent-scan (~/.sase/agent_artifact_index.sqlite). Same theme (unbounded append-only-ish store growth) but a different file, different subsystem, and different epic (sase-k3). Not a duplicate; a worker on either should be aware of the other for shared retention-policy conventions.

Triage sweep 2026-08-14 (requested by the project owner: keep the seven highest-impact open tasks, close the rest). All six are sase-l6 land-phase follow-ups on a path the epic already fixed with process-wide revalidating snapshot caches: store pruning/rotation, moving the artifact-file index into Rust indexed storage, scoping show_empty()'s cache clear, cold-cache re-measurement, auditing non-TUI read_artifact_file_index callers, and one bench budget (bench_tui_jk selected-tribe fold level 1, ~48 ms vs a 40 ms p95 budget on a 64-core host at loadavg ~30). No independent reporters, no user-visible defect. The one resolver kept open from this cluster is sase-lw, which measured 400-800 ms per TUI selection with no cache at all. Store growth stays visible: ~/.sase/artifacts/index.jsonl is 7.8 MB today -- re-file with a +1 and a fresh figure if it starts costing real latency.

payload.close_reason: Deprioritized in the 2026-08-14 task-backlog triage: epic sase-l6 already landed the SASE CONTEXT enrichment win these follow-ups refine.
